speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me exactly which antibiotic you were taking and when the rash and joint pain started relative to your last dose? I also need to know if you have any history of allergies or if the rash appears to be hives or a flat red discoloration.

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old girl. The patient was brought to the emergency department because of a 2-day history of low-grade fever, itchy rash, and generalized joint pain. The rash initially started in the antecubital and popliteal fossae before spreading to the trunk and distal extremities. One week ago, she was diagnosed with acute sinusitis and started on amoxicillin. She has no history of adverse drug reactions, and her immunizations are up to date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the rash blanch when you press on it, or does it look like small purple or red spots that do not fade? I also need to know if she has any swelling in her hands, feet, or around her eyes.

speaker: Doctor

speaker: Doctor
text: The rash is described as palpable purpura that does not blanch, which is highly suggestive of IgA vasculitis (Henoch-Schönlein purpura). I need to confirm if she has had any abdominal pain or joint swelling in her knees and ankles to support this diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis
